Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable.

Purpose

Financial Entities combines stable identity, lifecycle rules, permitted changes, and audit obligations. It describes what a continuing financial subject preserves over time. A composing domain supplies the concrete fields and business rules.

Documents

Start with identity, lifecycle, mutability, and validation. Continue with revisions, import, and evolution when retaining or changing existing records.

DocumentWhat you will learn
IdentityStable identity throughout a subject's lifecycle
LifecycleHow an Entity follows its Workflow
MutabilityWhich fields may change in each state
ValidationChecking the complete proposed Entity
RevisionsBusiness revisions and their distinction from conflict tokens
ImportPreserving existing identity, revisions, and explicit source mappings
EvolutionCorrection, reversal, void, and supersession with preserved evidence
ErrorsPortable failure codes and unchanged state after rejection

Requirements

A Financial Entity follows the canonical identity, lifecycle, mutability, validation, evolution, revisions, and import requirements.

  • ENTITY-AUDIT-001 — A composing domain MUST identify which Mutations and Transitions require an Audit Event.
    Evidence & context1 research note+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Preserving collected traces does not prove capture of required events ↗

    Surendra Kumar Valavala

    Core already requires Audit production for identified Entity changes and corresponding atomic evidence for portable evolution. The general coverage question cannot be used to call these existing obligations wholly deferred.

    Scope and limitations

    A separate expected workload can test coverage if it is independent of the collector. This is not a mandate to record every request or collect sensitive content indiscriminately. A diagnostic retry trace is not itself a unique financial effect.

  • ENTITY-AUDIT-002 — Each successful Mutation or Transition identified by ENTITY-AUDIT-001 MUST produce a corresponding Audit Event.

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Core already requires Audit production for identified Entity changes and corresponding atomic evidence for portable evolution. The general coverage question cannot be used to call these existing obligations wholly deferred.

    Scope and limitations

    A separate expected workload can test coverage if it is independent of the collector. This is not a mandate to record every request or collect sensitive content indiscriminately. A diagnostic retry trace is not itself a unique financial effect.

  • ENTITY-DEFINITION-001 — A composing domain MUST define its fields, lifecycle, and financially relevant invariants.
  • ENTITY-DEFINITION-002 — An existing Financial Entity MUST retain stable owned declarations for its lifecycle, mutability, and validation rules, including nested Workflow guards and declaration containers, whether the Workflow is versioned or unversioned. Mutating original constructor/import inputs or returned definition observations MUST NOT change the behavior of that existing Entity. Immutable representations and defensive copies MAY realize this guarantee.

Core 2.0 Entity Evolution defines portable correction, reversal, void, and supersession relations. Evolution preserves stable Entity identity and historical financial facts, uses explicit Entity Revision and Evolution Relation identities, requires caller-supplied Audit evidence, and rejects invalid or duplicate evolution without creating partial Entity, evolution, or Audit observations.

Core 2.0 Entity Revision and Import refines business revision observations and defines a bounded import boundary. Import preserves stable FinKore Entity identity, records explicit source identity mapping when external identity is present, preserves current and historical Entity Revision identity, keeps Entity Conflict Version distinct from business revision identity, and rejects stale expected-state/revision/conflict-version observations without partial import.

Invariants

A Financial Entity's identity must remain stable throughout its lifecycle. Its current State and data must reflect only successful domain operations.

Declaration ownership

ENTITY-DEFINITION-002 governs declarations retained for an existing Entity instance, including unversioned Workflows. It does not require stateless APIs to retain declarations across unrelated calls or define migration or dynamic reconfiguration.

Non-Goals

Core 2.0 does not define any concrete financial entity type, storage model, financial ownership model, global identity registry, deduplication service, authorization model, API, or user interface.
